plain_language_meaning: Red light and near-infrared devices are commonly described by wavelength, usually measured in nanometers. Different wavelengths may have different tissue interaction profiles, and wavelength alone does not define dose.
safety_note: Compare wavelength claims carefully. Wavelength should be interpreted with irradiance, distance, treatment area, and session duration.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Wavelength is a specification field, not a standalone dose claim.
source_name: Unlocking the Power of Light on the Skin: A Comprehensive Review on Photobiomodulation
citation_note: Use as broad review support for red and near-infrared wavelength terminology, skin-facing photobiomodulation context, and the distinction between red/NIR device categories. Do not use as a disease-treatment claim.

plain_language_meaning: Irradiance describes the light power delivered to an area, commonly expressed as milliwatts per square centimeter. Irradiance depends on device output, distance, beam angle, and measurement method.
safety_note: Irradiance should be interpreted only when distance and measurement conditions are disclosed.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Irradiance values can vary by testing method and distance.
source_name: Under the spotlight: mechanisms of photobiomodulation concentrating on blue and green light
citation_note: Use for the concept that photobiomodulation effects depend on radiometric parameters including wavelength, irradiance, dose, and delivered photons. Use as measurement-context support, not protocol guidance.

plain_language_meaning: Fluence describes energy delivered per unit area, commonly expressed as joules per square centimeter. Fluence depends on irradiance and exposure time. More is not automatically better.
safety_note: Avoid assuming that higher fluence or longer exposure automatically produces better results.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Fluence is a dose-related concept but should not be used as a treatment recommendation.
source_name: Dosimetry for photobiomodulation therapy: response to Sommers
citation_note: Use for dose/dosimetry caution and biphasic-response context. Supports the idea that more delivered energy is not automatically better.

plain_language_meaning: The distance between the device and the skin can strongly affect delivered light intensity. Compare devices only when distance and measurement conditions are disclosed.
safety_note: Distance changes delivered intensity, so dose comparisons should include measurement distance.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Distance is one of the most important missing details in many consumer device comparisons.
source_name: Photobiomodulation for pain relief: Model-based estimates of effective parameters
citation_note: Use for the idea that light reaching target tissue depends on optical properties and that tissue-level irradiance/fluence can differ from emitter output. Supports cautious distance and measurement-condition language.

plain_language_meaning: Session time is one component of delivered dose, but it should be interpreted with irradiance, area, and wavelength. Follow manufacturer instructions and avoid assuming longer sessions are always better.
safety_note: Follow manufacturer instructions and avoid extending sessions beyond recommended guidance.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Session duration should not be presented as a medical protocol.
source_name: Brain Photobiomodulation Therapy: A Narrative Review
citation_note: Use for biphasic dose-response context and the need to interpret exposure parameters carefully. Do not convert into session-length recommendations.

plain_language_meaning: Bright red or near-infrared lights may require eye-safety precautions depending on device design and exposure conditions. Follow manufacturer eye-protection instructions, especially for facial use or high-output devices.
safety_note: Eye protection guidance should follow manufacturer instructions, especially near the face or with high-output devices.
source_type: Safety guidance / consumer device use context
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: Eye safety language should stay cautious and non-medical.
source_name: Safety Profile of Slit-Lamp-Delivered Retinal Laser Photobiomodulation
citation_note: Use as eye/retina safety-context support showing that eye-facing photobiomodulation safety depends on wavelength, irradiance, delivery method, and controlled conditions. Keep manufacturer eye-protection language.

plain_language_meaning: Some devices may produce warmth or heat depending on output and session length. Stop use if discomfort, irritation, overheating, or unusual symptoms occur.
safety_note: Stop use if discomfort, irritation, overheating, or unusual symptoms occur.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: This is a comfort and safety caution, not treatment guidance.
source_name: Bio-Heat Transfer and Monte Carlo Measurement of Near-Infrared Transcranial Stimulation of Human Brain
citation_note: Use only as thermal/near-infrared modeling context showing that heat and tissue interaction are relevant considerations. Do not use as clinical proof or consumer protocol support.

plain_language_meaning: Useful red light device documentation should disclose wavelength, irradiance at distance, treatment area, recommended distance, and session guidance. A vague red light dose claim is less useful than clear device specifications.
safety_note: Consumers should be cautious when device pages make vague dose claims without clear specifications.
commercial_relevance: Red light masks / red light panels / red light wraps / consumer wellness devices
notes: This row supports transparent comparison without making clinical claims.
source_name: Photobiomodulation for pain relief: Model-based estimates of effective parameters
citation_note: Use to support specification transparency: wavelength, irradiance, fluence, tissue delivery assumptions, and measurement conditions should be disclosed when comparing devices.
